### C. Streak engine (W3)

Day facts that cannot be derived later are logged; the streak itself is always recomputed (invariant 4: blocked days come only from the badge evaluation's `activeDayStamps`, which come from the rollups or `NetEffectiveIntervals`). The streak runs INSIDE `BadgeCoordinator` (same triggers, including the 60-second live tick while a source runs and the midnight task, the same save chain, epoch guard, and wipe detection), and its log is stored inside `BadgeLedger`. No second coordinator and no second file.

`StreakLog` (`Shared/Models/StreakLog.swift`, `Codable, Equatable`), stored as the new lenient optional field `BadgeLedger.streakLog: StreakLog?` (added to `CodingKeys`; missing or corrupt decodes to nil, which re-initializes the log at today). Fields:
- `firstDay: String` (day stamp)
- `lastRecordedDay: String`
- `scheduledDays: Set<String>`
- `limitKeptDays: Set<String>`
- `weekPassAllowance: [String: Int]` (Sunday day stamp to 0, 1, or 2)

`StreakLogRecorder.record(_ log: StreakLog?, schedules: [BlockingSchedule], schedulesWithTargets: Set<UUID>, limits: [AppLimit], limitDayState: LimitDayState, now: Date, calendar: Calendar) -> StreakLog` (`Shared/Support/StreakLogRecorder.swift`, pure):
- nil log: create with `firstDay = lastRecordedDay = today`, then write today as a FIRST write.
- Days strictly after `lastRecordedDay` through today are FIRST writes from the current schedules and limits. `lastRecordedDay` itself is REWRITTEN only when it is still today (today stays provisional all day; a closed day is frozen). Then `lastRecordedDay = today`. If today is before `lastRecordedDay` (clock moved back), return the log unchanged.
- Scheduled(D): some schedule in `schedulesWithTargets` has `D`'s weekday in `activeDays` and a non-degenerate window that STARTS on D (an overnight window belongs to its start day) whose end is after the schedule's `createdAt`. On a REWRITE of today, a window that already ended before `now` marks today only if today was already in `scheduledDays` (edits keep `createdAt`, so an edit at 3 PM that adds today's weekday with a 9 to 10 AM window must not create a false miss).
- LimitKept(D): some `AppLimit` with `isEnabled`, a non-nil selection, and `createdAt` before the end of D, AND no limit was skipped or unlocked on D. For any day D being written, "skipped or unlocked" reads `limitDayState` when its `dayStamp` equals D's stamp (any entry with `skippedToday || unlockedToday`); any other stamp reads as no bypass (the store returns the last file even when stale, `SharedDataStore+Limits.swift:20-23`, which also covers a past day whose skip pass never saved before a kill). Skip and unlock are in-app actions, so a day the app never saw has no bypass.
- Week allowance: for every Sunday-start week touched by the written range with no entry, store `min(2, floor(n / 2))` where n counts the week's 7 days as scheduled: days before `firstDay` count as not scheduled, written days use the log, days after today use the current schedules. Never overwrite an existing entry.
- All day math uses `startOfDay` and `date(byAdding: .day, ...)` (invariant 3).

`StreakEngine` (`Shared/Support/StreakEngine.swift`, pure). Constants in `StreakConfig`: `maxPassesPerWeek = 2`, `rescueMinimumSeconds = 1800`, `rescueWindowDays = 2`, `rescueMinimumPlannedMinutes = 30`.

`StreakEngine.rescueStarts(completedQuick: [CompletedFocusSession], bypasses: [BypassEvent], gaps: [(start: Date, end: Date)], runningQuickStart: (start: Date, durationMinutes: Int)?, now: Date) -> [Date]` (a tuple, not `FocusSession`: `FocusSession.swift` is not in the test target; planned end = start + minutes x 60): the start of every completed Quick Start whose effective seconds (`NetEffectiveIntervals.intervals(blocks: [], quick: completedQuick, bypasses:, gaps:)` summed per `.quickStart(id)` source) are at least 1800, plus the running Quick Start's start when its `durationMinutes >= 30` and its planned end is after `now` (a running rescue already counts as saving; every pass re-walks, so if it ends early under 30 minutes the miss is pending or broken again on the next pass). Nothing else is a rescue. Deduplicate the returned starts (a session can briefly appear both running and completed). Before deriving, filter `completedQuick` to `startTime >= start of the day after log.firstDay` (no earlier start can rescue anything; this changes no result and keeps the per-tick cost flat).

`StreakEngine.evaluate(_ input: StreakInput) -> StreakStatus`. Input: `now`, `calendar`, `log`, `blockedDays: Set<String>` (the evaluation's `activeDayStamps`, which already include today's live tail, `BadgeEngine.swift:72-74, 189-191`), `liveSourceStart: Date?` (the running source's start, `inputs.activeStart`; when that is nil, the earliest `actualStart` among `store.loadActiveBlockSessions()` rows whose `plannedEnd <= now`, i.e. a block that ended but is not finalized yet, read in `loadInputs`; nil when neither exists), `vacations: [VacationPeriod]`, `rescueStarts: [Date]`, `noScheduledWindowLeftToday: Bool`.

Weeks run Sunday to Saturday regardless of the calendar's `firstWeekday`: week start = `startOfDay(D)` minus `(weekday(D) - 1)` days via `date(byAdding: .day, ...)`; never `dateInterval(of: .weekOfYear)`.

Walk each closed day D from `log.firstDay` through yesterday, then today:
- scheduled = `log.scheduledDays` contains D.
- counts = `blockedDays` contains D OR `log.limitKeptDays` contains D OR (`liveSourceStart` is before the start of D+1, for a closed D: a source still running past midnight blocked time on D, but its pre-midnight part is not in `blockedDays` until it finalizes, because the live tail is clamped to today).
- counts: run += 1.
- not counts, scheduled, not touched by a vacation (`VacationRules.touchesDay`), run > 0: a miss. If the week's passes used < allowance (missing entry reads 0): use a pass. Else take the earliest unused rescue start in `[start of D+1, start of D+3)`: one saves it; none and `now < start of D+3`: pending (at risk, deadline = start of D+3); none and the deadline passed: run = 0.
- not counts, run == 0: nothing.
- not counts, run > 0, not scheduled or vacation-touched: nothing (run unchanged).
- Today: counts adds 1; today is never a miss.
- Projection (feeds `riskDeadline` when no closed-day miss is pending): today is at risk when it is scheduled, not vacation-touched, does not count, the run is above 0, no pass is left this week, `noScheduledWindowLeftToday` is true, and `liveSourceStart` is nil (a source that just started counts today within a tick or two; the dot and alert must not linger meanwhile).

Output `StreakStatus: Equatable`: `current: Int`, `riskDeadline: Date?` (the earliest pending miss's deadline; when only the projection holds, `date(byAdding: .day, value: 3, to: startOfDay(now))`; nil otherwise), `isOnVacation: Bool` (a vacation in the input is active at `now`).

## Edge cases

| Case | Disposition |
|---|---|
| Clean count drops when late data lands (a pause recorded after the block's evaluation) | Count is derived and may fall by 1; milestones latch, so nothing re-celebrates. Accepted. |
| Two clean milestones crossed while away | Queue shows only the highest (W1 test). |
| Temporary-access mirror grows forever | One small record per grant (max 3 at once, 5 to 30 minutes each). Accepted. |
| Upgrade with 30 historical clean blocks | One "Clean x25" celebration, never a stack (W1 test). Pre-release test devices only. |
| Upgrade by a user who already earned Clean Session | The old code emptied the temporary-access mirror at that earn and the grants file keeps 48 hours, so older blocks that had temporary access re-judge as clean: the count after upgrade can come out slightly high, silently. Accepted (pre-release; only test devices hold such ledgers). |
| Clean milestone first detected while the app is briefly in the background, with no alert pre-scheduled | No immediate banner (`BadgeCoordinator.swift:403-409` posts only tier and achievement news); the celebration shows on the next open. Accepted. |
| Vacation started while a block runs | Refused with the block's end time (W2 visual + device step 5). |
| Overnight block running at 12:00 AM when vacation ends | Not shielded until the next app open (reconcile) or its next start; DeviceActivity cannot schedule a one-shot wake 14 days out. Accepted; the welcome-back alert prompts an open. |
| First block on the return day starts before 1:00 AM | Welcome-back alert clamps to the vacation end (12:00 AM). Accepted (W2 test). |
| User edits schedules during vacation | The return alert re-plans at the next foreground re-sync (`MainTabView.swift:320-325`), not instantly. Accepted. |
| Vacation ends automatically at 12:00 AM while the app stays open | `MainTabView`'s day-rollover task reloads `VacationController`'s stored `activeVacation`, clearing the banner, Settings text, and page state (W2); the Home icon follows the streak status at the midnight evaluation (W3 status, W4 icon). `endNow()` on a stale banner is a no-op (W2). |
| Start tapped while the UI is stale and a block just began | `start(returnDay:)` re-checks `activeScheduledBlock` from a fresh read and refuses (W2). |
| Pre-block reminders after an automatic vacation end | Come back at the next app open (foreground resync). Accepted (U16). |
| Vacation state in the extension | Read from App Group defaults through the same accessors (all-scheme build; device steps). |
| Return-day range across DST | `date(byAdding: .day)` (W2 test). |
| App not opened for 30 days | Recorder writes 30 days from current schedules and limits, which cannot have changed without the app; no skip or unlock is possible without the app. |
| Schedule deleted the same day to dodge a miss | A rewrite of today after the deletion drops today from `scheduledDays`. A block that ran already counts the day through its blocked time; deleting a schedule whose window passed without running dodges the miss. Accepted. |
| Limit skipped after the app's last evaluation of the day | Skip and unlock are in-app actions followed by a data-change post, so `BadgeCoordinator` re-evaluates right after. Accepted. |
| A kept limit makes every day count | User decision U5. With a limit on, the streak can only break on a day the user skips or unlocks a limit and blocks nothing. |
| Schedule edited mid-week shrinks that week's scheduled days | Allowance is frozen at first sight (W3 test). |
| Rescue Quick Start crosses the deadline | Start inside the window counts; while it runs the miss reads as saved; ended early under 30 minutes, the next pass re-walks to pending or broken (W3 test). |
| A user who missed today's block starts and immediately ends a vacation the same day | Any day a vacation touches is neutral (U8), so today cannot count against the streak. Same class as the accepted schedule-deletion dodge; a 30-minute Quick Start would count the day anyway. Accepted. |
| Non-Gregorian system calendar (Buddhist, Japanese) | The streak inherits the badge engine's stamp mismatch with the Gregorian rollup and limit-day stamps (badges are already affected). Accepted; a fix belongs to the badge engine. |
| Cold launch near 09:00 | `status` is nil until the first evaluation, so the foreground re-sync briefly removes a pending risk alert; it returns when the status lands. Lost only if the launch straddles 09:00. Accepted. |
| App opened on the return morning before the welcome-back alert | The alert is kept: `vacationEndsAt` still reports an automatic end from earlier today (W2 test, device step 10). |
| Block ended but not yet finalized (window over, `intervalDidEnd` or drain still pending) | `liveSourceStart` falls back to the unfinalized row's start, so the day stays counted and no false at-risk dot or alert appears (W3 test). |
| Block starting exactly at the return-day midnight | `inactiveScheduleIDs` treats the vacation as over within `occurrenceMatchToleranceSeconds` of its end (W2). |
| Overnight block still running after midnight | `liveSourceStart` keeps its start day counted until it finalizes (W3 test). |
| Two pending misses | Each needs its own Quick Start; the earliest deadline drives the alert (W3 test). |
| Clock moved backwards | Recorder no-op (W3 test). |
| Time zone change | Day stamps use the current calendar, as badges do. Accepted. |
| Delete All Data | Container wipe removes `badge_ledger.json` (with the streak log inside); the vacation key is wiped by the registry; `BadgeCoordinator`'s existing wipe detection drops queued saves. |
| Ledger write fails | The in-memory ledger (with the streak log) stays authoritative, as for badges today. Accepted. |
| Notifications off | Risk, vacation-return, and recap specs are gated by the existing master toggle. |
| 4-digit streak | Fixed 15 pt font; the toolbar item grows; verified in W4 with `NUDGE_STREAK_PREVIEW=long`. |

- U3. The Saturday recap gains a clean-blocks clause (the recap already exists).
- U4. No pause-screen line now (parked for later).
- U5. A day counts toward the streak when it had any effective blocked time, OR at least one daily limit was on that day and none was skipped or unlocked that day ("stayed within their limit"). This applies on scheduled days too, so a kept limit also protects a scheduled day.
- U6. Passes per Sunday to Saturday week: 0 with 1 scheduled day, 1 with 2 or 3, 2 with 4 or more (`min(2, floor(n / 2))`). Used automatically on a missed scheduled day. A week's allowance is frozen the first time the app sees that week.
- U7. Rescue: a missed scheduled day with no pass left is "at risk". One Quick Start with at least 30 minutes of effective blocked time, started after the missed day ended and before the start of day D+3 (local calendar; "within 48 hours"), saves it. One Quick Start saves one missed day. A saved or pass-covered day adds nothing and breaks nothing. A miss while the streak is 0 is never at risk. Saving a streak earns no badge.
- U8. Vacation: at most 14 days. Starts immediately, only when no scheduled block is enforcing (never cuts a running block short). The user picks the return day (tomorrow up to today + 14); blocks come back at 12:00 AM that day. Quick Starts and daily limits keep working. Free. No cooldown.
- U9. Welcome-back notification only when the vacation ends automatically: it fires at whichever is earlier, 9:00 AM on the return day or 1 hour before the first scheduled block that starts on the return day, but never before the vacation's end. Ending vacation manually cancels it and sends nothing.
- U10. The Home streak indicator is display-only: tapping it does nothing. No streak sheet.
- U11. No badge for saving a streak; the Achievements grid stays at 15 with one empty slot in the last row.
- U12. The four Active Days badges are renamed "<n> Days Total" so they don't read like streak numbers.
- U13. Analytics: `vacation_started` (days) and `vacation_ended_early` (days_left).
- U14. Streak tracking starts on the first day the new code runs; earlier history is not back-filled.
- U15. The streak-at-risk notification fires at the next 9:00 AM before the rescue deadline.
- U16. Pre-block reminders are cancelled while a vacation is active and come back at the first app open after it ends. Win-back notifications that would fire before the vacation's end are dropped.

## Design

### A. Clean repeat badge (W1)

Rule. A completed session is CLEAN when it meets every existing `hasCleanSession` condition AND its planned length is at least `BadgeConfig.cleanBlockMinimumSeconds` (3600):
- Scheduled block: `CountableSession.includes`, `actualEnd` present, `endReason` nil or `.naturalEnd`, reached planned end within `SharedConstants.occurrenceMatchToleranceSeconds`, started within `cleanSessionStartGraceSeconds` of planned start, zero overlap with pauses, enforcement gaps, and temporary-access spans inside the clamped window, and `plannedEnd - plannedStart >= 3600`.
- Quick Start: `plannedDurationMinutes` present and `* 60 >= 3600`, reached its planned end within tolerance, zero overlap.

Count. `BadgeEngine.cleanSessionEndDates(_ data: BadgeSourceData) -> [Date]` returns the end date of every clean session (replaces `hasCleanSession`): for a block `min(actualEnd, plannedEnd)`, for a Quick Start `min(endTime, startTime + plannedDurationMinutes x 60)` (invariant 2: a late callback never moves a clean block across the 7-day boundary). Build the holes array ONCE per call, sorted by start; for each session check only the holes whose start is before the session's clamped end (the count now scans every session on the main actor every 60-second live tick, where `hasCleanSession` stopped at the first). `BadgeEvaluation` gains `cleanCount: Int` (the array's count) and `cleanCountLast7Days: Int` (end dates on or after `calendar.date(byAdding: .day, value: -6, to: calendar.startOfDay(for: now))`, the window `ChartDataCalculator.dailyEffectiveData` uses (`ChartDataCalculator.swift:51-54`) and so the one behind `last7DaysProtectedSeconds`). The count is derived from source data on every evaluation (accounting invariant 4); only milestones latch.

Temporary-access mirror. Re-judging all history every evaluation needs grants older than the 48-hour pruned grants file, so `BadgeLedger.temporaryAccessRecords` is now kept forever: delete the "clear once cleanSession is earned" branch and the "stays empty once earned" behavior; keep the upsert-by-grant-id.

Milestones. `BadgeConfig.isCleanMilestone(_ n: Int) -> Bool` (1, 10, 25, 50, 100, then every multiple of 100), `BadgeConfig.nextCleanMilestone(after count: Int) -> Int`, `BadgeConfig.highestCleanMilestone(atOrBelow count: Int) -> Int` (0 when count < 1).

Ledger (additive, lenient-decoded like every other optional field, added to `CodingKeys`), two high-water marks in the style of the per-month tier latch and celebrated pair (`BadgeLedger.swift:24-32`):
- `cleanMilestoneReached: Int` (default 0)
- `cleanMilestoneCelebrated: Int` (default 0)

Reconcile. `cleanMilestoneReached = max(cleanMilestoneReached, highestCleanMilestone(atOrBelow: cleanCount))` (a count that later dips never lowers it). No adoption step: the queue only ever shows the highest milestone, so an upgraded test device sees at most one "Clean x<n>" celebration, the same way achievements queue on an initial pass.

Queue. `CelebrationItem` gains `.clean(milestone: Int)` with id `"clean-<n>"`. `celebrationQueue` emits `.clean(cleanMilestoneReached)` only when it is greater than `cleanMilestoneCelebrated`; it sits after achievements and before tier steps. `markCelebrated(.clean(n))` sets `cleanMilestoneCelebrated = max(cleanMilestoneCelebrated, n)`.

Celebration copy (reuse the achievement celebration layout and the existing Clean coin art; eyebrow stays "BADGE EARNED"):
- Title: "Clean" when n == 1, else "Clean x<n>".
- Subtitle: n == 1: "A block of 1 hour or more, start to finish, no pause." Else: "<n> blocks of 1 hour or more, start to finish, no pause."
- Next line (same slot and style as achievement `nextHint`): "Next: Clean x<next milestone>."
- Achieved-bar pill: "x<n>".
- Share card line: "Clean x<n> earned with BestSpent." (n == 1: "Clean earned with BestSpent.")
- `celebrationShared(kind:)` passes "clean".
- `ReviewPromptPolicy.qualifies` returns false for clean items.

Prediction. `PredictedCrossing.Kind` gains `.clean(milestone: Int)`. Predict at `plannedEnd` when the running session is on time, has no pause so far, has no active pause, its planned length is at least 3600 s, `cleanCount + 1` is a milestone, and `cleanCount + 1 > cleanMilestoneReached` (no repeat alert after a dip and climb back). Planned length is `plannedEnd - plannedStart`, never measured from the session's (clamped) `start`. Plumbing: `RunningBadgeSession.plannedStart: Date?` (nil means no clean prediction); `BadgeEngine.runningSession(...)` (`BadgeEngine.swift:760-806`) gains a `plannedStart: Date?` parameter and passes it through; `EvalInputs` gains `runningSourcePlannedStart: Date?`, set in `BadgeCoordinator.loadInputs` from the active Quick Start's `startTime`, or for a block from the matching occurrence rows' `plannedStart` (the same rows `runningSourceStartedOnTime` matches; no row gives nil); the call at `BadgeCoordinator.swift:360-370` passes it. Existing callers of `runningSession` to update: the helpers in `BadgeEngineRunningSessionTests`, `BadgeEngineLiveTailSecondsTests.swift:72-82`, and `BadgeEngineTests.swift:993-1000`. Notification identifier `"<badge_crossing>-clean-<n>"`, body "Badge earned: Clean." for n == 1, else "Badge earned: Clean x<n>."

Catalog. Delete `AchievementID.cleanSession`, `AchievementRequirement.cleanSession`, and its catalog row: the catalog has 15 achievements. Old ledgers keep the `"cleanSession"` string; readers already ignore unknown achievement strings. The coin drawing is keyed by `AchievementID` today (`AchievementCoin.swift:28`, `palette(for:)` 136-138, `showsGlow` 144, `AchievementCoinGlyph(id:)`, the exhaustive `AchievementGlyphLibrary.drawing(for:)` 72-90). Give it a key `enum CoinArt { case achievement(AchievementID), clean }`; the palette, glow, and glyph lookups switch on it, with `.clean` mapping to the old cleanSession palette (`AchievementCoin.swift:286-290`, moved verbatim) and `sparkle()` (`AchievementGlyphLibrary.swift:83`). `BadgeView.Art` gains `.clean`, routed to that coin; for `.clean`, `assetName` is nil and the accessibility name is "Clean". The earned and locked art must be byte-for-byte the old Clean Session art (the W1 reviewer diffs the moved palette and glyph code). Rename the Active Days rows: displayName "3 Days Total", "7 Days Total", "14 Days Total", "30 Days Total"; nextHint "Next: 7 days total.", "Next: 14 days total.", "Next: 30 days total."; shortName "3 Days Total", "7 Days Total", "14 Days Total", "30 Days Total" (the grid caption reads `shortName`, `BadgesScreen.swift:228`; they fit two lines at 12 pt in the 78 pt cell); description unchanged.

Presenter. `BadgeUIState` gains `clean: CleanBadgeState` (`count: Int`, `nextMilestone: Int`) and `cleanCountLast7Days: Int`. Mock scenarios in `BadgeViewModel.swift` get counts: `.dayOne` 0, `.preMonthly` 3, `.midMonthClimber` 24.

Recap. `EngagementFacts` gains `last7DaysCleanBlocks: Int`. `weeklyRecapSpec` body:
- 0: unchanged.
- 1: "You had at least <X> back and 1 clean block in the 7 days to <weekday>. Come see what this week added."
- n > 1: "You had at least <X> back and <n> clean blocks in the 7 days to <weekday>. Come see what this week added."
`MainTabView` reads the live badge state's `cleanCountLast7Days` for the fact and adds it to `engagementFactsKey`.

### C. Streak engine (W3)

Day facts that cannot be derived later are logged; the streak itself is always recomputed (invariant 4: blocked days come only from the badge evaluation's `activeDayStamps`, which come from the rollups or `NetEffectiveIntervals`). The streak runs INSIDE `BadgeCoordinator` (same triggers, including the 60-second live tick while a source runs and the midnight task, the same save chain, epoch guard, and wipe detection), and its log is stored inside `BadgeLedger`. No second coordinator and no second file.

`StreakLog` (`Shared/Models/StreakLog.swift`, `Codable, Equatable`), stored as the new lenient optional field `BadgeLedger.streakLog: StreakLog?` (added to `CodingKeys`; missing or corrupt decodes to nil, which re-initializes the log at today). Fields:
- `firstDay: String` (day stamp)
- `lastRecordedDay: String`
- `scheduledDays: Set<String>`
- `limitKeptDays: Set<String>`
- `weekPassAllowance: [String: Int]` (Sunday day stamp to 0, 1, or 2)

`StreakLogRecorder.record(_ log: StreakLog?, schedules: [BlockingSchedule], schedulesWithTargets: Set<UUID>, limits: [AppLimit], limitDayState: LimitDayState, now: Date, calendar: Calendar) -> StreakLog` (`Shared/Support/StreakLogRecorder.swift`, pure):
- nil log: create with `firstDay = lastRecordedDay = today`, then write today as a FIRST write.
- Days strictly after `lastRecordedDay` through today are FIRST writes from the current schedules and limits. `lastRecordedDay` itself is REWRITTEN only when it is still today (today stays provisional all day; a closed day is frozen). Then `lastRecordedDay = today`. If today is before `lastRecordedDay` (clock moved back), return the log unchanged.
- Scheduled(D): some schedule in `schedulesWithTargets` has `D`'s weekday in `activeDays` and a non-degenerate window that STARTS on D (an overnight window belongs to its start day) whose end is after the schedule's `createdAt`. On a REWRITE of today, a window that already ended before `now` marks today only if today was already in `scheduledDays` (edits keep `createdAt`, so an edit at 3 PM that adds today's weekday with a 9 to 10 AM window must not create a false miss).
- LimitKept(D): some `AppLimit` with `isEnabled`, a non-nil selection, and `createdAt` before the end of D, AND no limit was skipped or unlocked on D. For any day D being written, "skipped or unlocked" reads `limitDayState` when its `dayStamp` equals D's stamp (any entry with `skippedToday || unlockedToday`); any other stamp reads as no bypass (the store returns the last file even when stale, `SharedDataStore+Limits.swift:20-23`, which also covers a past day whose skip pass never saved before a kill). Skip and unlock are in-app actions, so a day the app never saw has no bypass.
- Week allowance: for every Sunday-start week touched by the written range with no entry, store `min(2, floor(n / 2))` where n counts the week's 7 days as scheduled: days before `firstDay` count as not scheduled, written days use the log, days after today use the current schedules. Never overwrite an existing entry.
- All day math uses `startOfDay` and `date(byAdding: .day, ...)` (invariant 3).

`StreakEngine` (`Shared/Support/StreakEngine.swift`, pure). Constants in `StreakConfig`: `maxPassesPerWeek = 2`, `rescueMinimumSeconds = 1800`, `rescueWindowDays = 2`, `rescueMinimumPlannedMinutes = 30`.

`StreakEngine.rescueStarts(completedQuick: [CompletedFocusSession], bypasses: [BypassEvent], gaps: [(start: Date, end: Date)], runningQuickStart: (start: Date, durationMinutes: Int)?, now: Date) -> [Date]` (a tuple, not `FocusSession`: `FocusSession.swift` is not in the test target; planned end = start + minutes x 60): the start of every completed Quick Start whose effective seconds (`NetEffectiveIntervals.intervals(blocks: [], quick: completedQuick, bypasses:, gaps:)` summed per `.quickStart(id)` source) are at least 1800, plus the running Quick Start's start when its `durationMinutes >= 30` and its planned end is after `now` (a running rescue already counts as saving; every pass re-walks, so if it ends early under 30 minutes the miss is pending or broken again on the next pass). Nothing else is a rescue. Deduplicate the returned starts (a session can briefly appear both running and completed). Before deriving, filter `completedQuick` to `startTime >= start of the day after log.firstDay` (no earlier start can rescue anything; this changes no result and keeps the per-tick cost flat).

`StreakEngine.evaluate(_ input: StreakInput) -> StreakStatus`. Input: `now`, `calendar`, `log`, `blockedDays: Set<String>` (the evaluation's `activeDayStamps`, which already include today's live tail, `BadgeEngine.swift:72-74, 189-191`), `liveSourceStart: Date?` (the running source's start, `inputs.activeStart`; when that is nil, the earliest `actualStart` among `store.loadActiveBlockSessions()` rows whose `plannedEnd <= now`, i.e. a block that ended but is not finalized yet, read in `loadInputs`; nil when neither exists), `vacations: [VacationPeriod]`, `rescueStarts: [Date]`, `noScheduledWindowLeftToday: Bool`.

Weeks run Sunday to Saturday regardless of the calendar's `firstWeekday`: week start = `startOfDay(D)` minus `(weekday(D) - 1)` days via `date(byAdding: .day, ...)`; never `dateInterval(of: .weekOfYear)`.

Walk each closed day D from `log.firstDay` through yesterday, then today:
- scheduled = `log.scheduledDays` contains D.
- counts = `blockedDays` contains D OR `log.limitKeptDays` contains D OR (`liveSourceStart` is before the start of D+1, for a closed D: a source still running past midnight blocked time on D, but its pre-midnight part is not in `blockedDays` until it finalizes, because the live tail is clamped to today).
- counts: run += 1.
- not counts, scheduled, not touched by a vacation (`VacationRules.touchesDay`), run > 0: a miss. If the week's passes used < allowance (missing entry reads 0): use a pass. Else take the earliest unused rescue start in `[start of D+1, start of D+3)`: one saves it; none and `now < start of D+3`: pending (at risk, deadline = start of D+3); none and the deadline passed: run = 0.
- not counts, run == 0: nothing.
- not counts, run > 0, not scheduled or vacation-touched: nothing (run unchanged).
- Today: counts adds 1; today is never a miss.
- Projection (feeds `riskDeadline` when no closed-day miss is pending): today is at risk when it is scheduled, not vacation-touched, does not count, the run is above 0, no pass is left this week, `noScheduledWindowLeftToday` is true, and `liveSourceStart` is nil (a source that just started counts today within a tick or two; the dot and alert must not linger meanwhile).

# Animations

Before adding any animation, check MOTION.md's Graveyard: killed
animations stay dead. This skill supplies the motion spec and the taste
bar; the repository's agent instructions decide who writes the code and
how it is verified.

## Curves

- Arrivals ease out. A **clock-driven** value gliding between two
  on-screen states eases in-out (`minuteTickGlide`, `chartRescale`,
  `blockListDigitRoll`); a **user-driven** change still eases out
  (`onboardingSelection`, `rangeBarMorph`). Linear is only for functional
  fills (hold sweeps, playback progress) and `duration: 0` instant
  resets. Symmetric opacity crossfades may ease in-out
  (`focusScreenAppear`).
- Springs are punctuation, not grammar: pops (`onboardingStampPop`,
  `newPillPop`), the one signature lift (`onboardingWordRoll`), and
  device-tuned settles (`topBarSpring`, `badgeMorph`,
  `tierPromotionSwap`). If you can't name what the overshoot celebrates
  or lands, ease out instead.
- Continuous indicators derive their phase from the wall clock under a
  timeline, never `@State` + `repeatForever`, so a re-render can never
  restart them (`ChartPulsingRing`, `LiveDotPulse`, `FloatingBadge`).
  Under Reduce Motion they stop moving: a static form or gone.
  Out-and-back accents are finite: they end on the value they started
  from and stop. Pre-skill deviations are recorded in MOTION.md's
  Screens entries, never here; flag one when nearby, don't detour.

## Timing

- Narrative blocks arrive at reading pace: each waits out the previous
  block's read hold, at the times `OnboardingStoryPacing` gives it, via
  `.onboardingEntrance(at:)` applied as the block's last modifier.
  Blocks that are one thought keep the old overlap, a gap of a third to
  a half of the entrance duration (`OnboardingStoryPacing.pairBeat`).
- Micro-cascades inside one block stay fast: one stagger token per
  surface, or a fixed span divided by item count when the count varies.
  Never the narrative beat.
- The payoff waits for the punch: a dependent reveal keys on the moment
  it answers, never on a fixed slot that can race it. A signature
  animation starts only after its own container is visibly present.
- Tab switches are near-cuts (`tabSwitchFade`). Opening a screen never
  replays history or animates live values into place: live ticks gate
  behind a quiet window (`liveTickQuietWindow`) and key on
  minute-granularity values, never a per-second clock.

## Rules

- Layout stability is inviolable: nothing outside the animating element
  may shift, reflow, or wrap. Reserve final width before animating
  (constant digit counts + `monospacedDigit` for rolls).
- Confetti is unique: one celebration overlay app-wide.
- Haptics use the five roles in `Haptics.swift` and nothing else:
  `.tap` to open, `.selection` to pick, `.success`/`.warning` when
  something actually committed, `.error` when it failed. A haptic may
  punctuate one motion beat that lands (a droplet, an odometer parking),
  never sprinkled through an animation, and Reduce Motion skips it,
  because a tick with nothing behind it is a tick from nowhere.
- Reduce Motion: settled on frame one (`reduceMotion ? nil : animation`
  + a static branch in body). Fades and functional fills may remain.
- Meaningful commits get a press-and-hold whose fill and completion
  clock read one duration constant, with a direct accessibility
  activation.
- Every **new** duration lives once: a token in DSAnimations.swift
  whose doc lists its riders. Share a token only when every rider should
  retune together; otherwise give the surface its own token and say why.
  Pre-skill surfaces still carry inline literals; leave them unless the
  task is theirs.

## Workflow

1. Check DSAnimations.swift and MOTION.md's Screens/Tokens entries for
   an existing answer before inventing values.
2. Implement per [references/mechanics.md](references/mechanics.md):
   read it before writing any SwiftUI animation.
3. Prove timing by measurement: screen-record, verify starts
   frame-by-frame and that no pixel outside the animating element
   changes.
4. Update MOTION.md in its existing shape: a `## Screens` entry, tokens
   under `## Tokens`, cuts under `## Graveyard` (permanent), and claim
   `## Signature` only for the app's one signature moment (the file
   names the incumbent).

## Edge cases
# tools/sim

Generic helpers for the build-and-test gate and for checking screens on the test
simulator. They know nothing about individual screens: you pass the labels,
settings and regions, read from the code and the plan. App facts (simulator ID,
UI-only scheme and bundle, App Group, build and test commands) are read from
`CLAUDE.md`, so the scripts follow it when it changes.

Every script prints `--help`, and every failure stops with a message saying what
it expected. If a script breaks because the app or a tool changed, fix the script
in place and say so in your report, so the fix sticks for the next wave.

| Script | Does | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `gate` | The CLAUDE.md gate, in order, printing the proof lines and the xcresult test count | `tools/sim/gate` (or `--presentation`, `--comment-only`, `--builds-only`) |
| `app` | Build, install and launch the UI-only app; write, remove, show and restore its settings | `tools/sim/app build && tools/sim/app launch`, `tools/sim/app set isProUser=true` |
| `tap` | Tap by accessibility label, swipe, type, wait for a label, list what is on screen | `tools/sim/tap "Settings" --expect "Shield screens"` |
| `shot` | Screenshot, optionally beside a mock at the same scale | `tools/sim/shot /tmp/home.png --compare mock.png --mock-scale 1.5` |
| `measure` | Rows or columns of content in an image, in points | `tools/sim/measure /tmp/home.png --region 0,100,402,400` |
| `record` | Record a few seconds and report when each region starts and stops moving | `tools/sim/record 3 /tmp/rec --then 'tools/sim/tap "Continue"' --region title=16,90,386,140` |

## A typical screen check

```sh
tools/sim/app build                      # after editing Swift code
tools/sim/app launch                     # installs the newest build and opens it
tools/sim/tap --list                     # confirm the first screen is the one you expect
tools/sim/tap "Settings" --expect "Shield screens"
tools/sim/shot /tmp/shield.png --compare /path/to/mock.png
tools/sim/measure /tmp/shield.png        # and the mock with --scale 1.5, then compare
```

## Things these scripts already handle

- Settings only stick when written while the simulator is shut down, and only
  through plistlib. `app set` does that, reads the file back to prove it, and
  prints a restore command. Always restore when you finish.
- The UI-only app keeps its App Group defaults inside its own data container.
- A stale build shows old code: `app launch` warns when the build is older than
  your latest source edit.
- `tap "Label"` prefers an exact label, then any label containing the text,
  on screen before off screen, and refuses to tap something scrolled off screen.
- `record` warns when Reduce Motion is on, since animations then do not play,
  ignores the status-bar clock, clears old frames from a reused folder, and
  fails if its `--then` command fails.
- Settings backups survive a reinstall: `app restore` finds the app's current
  data folder, which moves on every install.
- This Xcode prints no `Executed N tests` line: `gate` reads the counts from the
  result bundle.
- xcodebuild reorders `project.pbxproj`: `gate` reverts that only when the file
  had no changes of its own before the gate ran.

## Watch out for

- A seeded onboarding resume blob that fails to decode looks like "no blob" and
  starts onboarding fresh. Confirm the first screen with `tap --list` before
  trusting anything else in the run.
- Plan mocks are usually 1.5x renders; pass the plan's stated scale to `shot
  --mock-scale` and `measure --scale`.
